title: Commercial Law: sales and secured transactions
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Apply UCC Article 2 (formation, terms, warranties, risk of loss, performance and remedies) and Article 9 (attachment, perfection, priority and default), with an introduction to how bankruptcy treats secured creditors.

weeks.1: The scope of Article 2 and formation
weeks.2: Terms, the battle of the forms and parol evidence
weeks.7: The scope of Article 9 and attachment
weeks.8: Perfection by filing, possession and control
weeks.10: Purchase-money security interests and buyers in the ordinary course

blocks.deliverable: Allocate the risk of loss in four shipping scenarios.
Week 7 midterm; decide whether a security interest attached and is perfected.
Rank four competing claims to collateral.
Analyze a repossession and a deficiency claim.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Commercial transaction file: for a supplied inventory-financing deal and a later dispute, draft key security-agreement terms, check perfection, rank the creditors, and write a client memo.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
